That mechanism is actually only semi-automatic. If an error is made, the typist presses the correction key which also activates backspace. The mechanism then switches in to correction mode and the typist then presses the key corresponding to the ERROR made. The correction mechanism then lifts off (or on fabric ribbons which are no longer available for the IBM cover up) the error. The machine then goes back into normal typing mode where the typist can then type the correct character.

Now on modern electronic typewriters (such as the IBM Wheelwriter series and most machines made today) pressing correct will automatically perform the correction from electronic memory. On my Brother if I type "wos this is cool" I would backspace until I'm over the s, press correct and then w (and I don't have to wait on the machine it will buffer the keypress in memory) and then activate the Reloc(ate) function. On the correcting Selectric I would have to backspace to the space after the error, press correct, press s, then press w). Now if I need to go back to a previous line on my Brother I do have to do a similar procedure, first I would activate Rev 2 times (Rev goes back a half line, index advances a half line) move the carrier over the error, press CODE + Correct, type the error character (correct won't work, only the current line stays in memory) then type the correct character, then move back to where I was.

Pros/Cons of Voat Cost Saving Measure: Compress comment chains into a single db record

• Less server load to build the comment trees.
  • Less DB space used
  • Less API calls on voting up/down comments

• Nested replies get ugly fast, as it would all cascade linearly.
  • Can't upvoat/downvoat comments.
  • Max comment size on a chain of comments would be stricter since its all in one field.
  • Slightly more complicated validation to ensure users are only adding to the end of a comment not editing anything.

Celko nested sets would be most efficient and maintain the ability to infinitely nest records. The only cost is recalculation on the upsert...

If I were to do this, I'd have a key for the thread ID the post goes with and then have a left/right val for each thread:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nested_set_model

You should also probably consider whatever model is in place for the voats/karma/comment relationships as that data may be stored discretely to avoid cheating as much as possible since everyone only counts one vote per item.

I think it's a really bad idea to consider doing this. You're actually gaining nothing via this method and may actually be introducing significant processing overhead. You would be better off setting up a caching mechanism and using redis or memcachedb to store prerendered html snippets for the most often accessed parent comments, which itself is pretty substantial.
